newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't sees sugar exports at 5.4 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't sees sugar exports at 5.4 mln tonnes.

text.p: Brazilian sugar exports should total 5.4 million tonnes according to the 1997/98 sugar crop plan to be published Wednesday in the government's official gazette, said a top Industry and Commerce Ministry official.
"The number for exports in the crop plan is 5.4 million tonnes," said Mauricio Assis, head of the ministry's primary commodities department.
Despite expectations of higher sugar cane output, the exports are only slightly higher than the 5.2 million tonnes allocated in the 1996/97 crop plan.
This is because the government plans to use the extra sugar cane production to increase alcohol output, Assis said.
This year the government wants to boost alcohol production to the extent that imports are no longer necessary.
Assis said total sugar output this year should be around 14 million tonnes but he declined to give any further details of forecasts contained in the crop plan.
The crop plan will be published just before the traditional May 1 start to the center-south harvest which runs to November.
In the country's other producing region, the north/northeast, the harvest runs from September to April.
